1.why: Every MFA route passes through auth(), which binds the session cookie to account.id, and suppliedIdentifier() rejects any client-supplied user identifiers, so MFA settings are exclusively session-derived.

2.why: OTP verification is checked only against the per-account pending secret inside the authenticated session and is marked used on success, so a code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: Login deletes any prior session (sessions.delete(old)) and issues a fresh token, so previous sessions do not remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt(secret)) and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hash plus AES-GCM ciphertext, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, session tokens, CSRF tokens, TOTP seeds, and recovery codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and the client keeps the CSRF token and state only in in-memory variables; no localStorage, sessionStorage, or readable cookies are used.

7.why: The server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), recovery-code format, JSON content-type and size, and uses in-memory storage with no SQL queries.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered through esc()/textContent and a per-response nonce CSP (script-src 'nonce-...') blocks execution of injected markup or script.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all and client navigation is limited to fixed internal hash routes, so no open or user-controlled redirect exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: The session cookie is set as 'bank_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' on login and cleared the same way on logout.

12.why: Server errors are generic and no secrets appear in URLs or server logs, but the client-side log() writes the OTP seed, test OTP, and recovery codes into the on-page 'Logs' panel and browser console.

13.why: Pending codes carry a 5-minute expires and a used flag enforced in /api/mfa/verify, and recovery codes are marked used on redemption.

14.why: Five failed OTP attempts set p.locked and five failed recovery attempts set account.recoveryLocked, each imposing a 10-minute lockout.

15.why: Login rotates the session identifier (old deleted, new random token), auth() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
